**2\. Information on eligible costs**

**2.1 Relationship PI \- HI**

The project has three participating Institutions: CNR, which has been the hosting institution till October 2021, UNI Pisa, and Scuola Normale Superiore, which has taken the role of hosting Institution since November 2021\. The involvement of SNS in the project made the change of hosting Institution very smooth. The relationship between the Principal Investigator and the Host Institution (old and new) and also the other partner Institutions, has evolved as planned, and the provisions of the Supplementary Agreement have been respected. CNR has added extra resources to the project, in particular Daniele Fadda taking care of the XAI website and Andrea Beretta taking care of ethical deliverables, both supported by other funds that were allowed to support XAI in this last RP; University of Pisa and SNS have attracted many new PhD students with scholarships on institutional funds and many master students with theses on XAI arguments. SNS has also provided funds for a new postdoc, Martino Ciaperoni, selected through an international competition, currently involved in experimenting with ILLUME in complex biomedical problems. He is part of the team that has proposed the PoC ILLUME4Science

The **PI, Fosca Giannotti**, and the **co-PI, Dino Pedreschi**, participate in and supervise all RAs. Their effort has also been dedicated **to** establishing and cultivating collaborations with **several AI-relevant** H2020 AI projects, **specifically** the ICT48 network of excellence **Humane-AI-net**, TAILOR, the EU Research Infrastructure **SoBigData**, and the new nation-wide Italian project on AI named FAIR (Future AI Research). In particular, the spoke of Pisa is focused on **Human-Centered AI**. This provided the opportunity to demonstrate and make available **many of the project's achievements for joint use cases** to the Italian AI scientific community. This has also **led to** a new line of research formalized as **"Human-AI Coevolution"** in the paper published in *Artificial Intelligence*, Volume 339, February 2025, 104244\.  
   

**2.1.1 SNS: Team members and their activities in the RP**

Other than the PI, Fosca Giannotti, in the RP are involved:

* **Roberto Pellungrini** is an Assistant Professor recruited by SNS in November 2022\. **In RA1**, he has contributed to the evolution of our **XAI algorithms** in a hybrid decision-making setting. This contribution has **resulted in** a survey paper currently under evaluation and two ongoing papers (co-authored with two PhD students, Clara Punzi and Leitao, and the postdoc Bonsignori) focusing on explaining uncertainty and relative abstaining methods.[^2] He also **co-supervises** PhD students working on the theoretical foundation of XAI. **In RA4**, he contributed to the **ensemble method for counterfactual explanations in churn prediction \[83\]**[^3]..He is also a **Teaching Assistant**, following student projects for the PhD course **"Explainable AI"**. This involves **20 hours of lectures**, **20 hours of laboratory activities**, and project supervision at SNS.  
* **Prof.  Stefano Marmi** contributes to the RA1 and RA2 on studies of the theoretical foundation of interpretable by design approaches for deep learning architectures, contributing to the extension of the initial work on “Mathematical Foundation of Interpretable Equivariant Surrogate Models” \[105\]. 

Postdoc recruited:

* **Margherita Lalli** was recruited in July 2023, with a background in theoretical physics. She completed her PhD during the project. Her focus is on new inference methods between urn models and Bayesian ones that may be natively interpretable RA1. With the PhD student Gabriele Barlacchi, (hired on Institutional funds), she is focusing on creating a simulation environment to explore the various facets of the coevolution of the human-machine interaction[^4]. In RA4 she has been working in the team for applying ILLUME[^5] as a “XAI4Science” tool by applying it to complex biomedical problems, specifically in pharmacology and cancer research. She collaborates with expert biomedical scientists to show how ILLUME can provide valuable insights and new hypotheses where explanation is often more crucial than prediction. She is part of the team that has proposed the PoC ILLUME4Science.  
* **Marzio Di Vece** was recruited in July 2023, with a background on theoretical physics he completed her PhD during the project. In RA4 he contributed to developing an ensemble approach for generating counterfactual explanations to improve churn analysis interpretability\[83\]. He also worked on methods to project multivariate time series onto signed graphs, ensuring inherent explainability and enhancing transparency in complex systems analysis with the goal of delivering a methodology for Interpretable-by-Design Models for Business Networks as summarized in the technical report[^6].   
* **Giovanni Mauro** was recruited in October 2024\. He has completed complete his PhD in Spring 2025 on topics related to generative AI for understanding human mobility. The goal is to study the transformation of urban ecosystems, and this might turn into an interesting use case for RA4.[^7]  
* **Valerio Bonsignori** was recruited in October 2024\. He will complete his PhD in few months on explainability for federated learning (RA1), and this has produced few initial papers on Differentially Private FastSHAP for Federated Learning Model Explanations [^8]. He has also started to work on the method L2R-CE for Explaining the Reject Option (RA1), and on RA4 applying XAI method in Healthcare: Post Ictus Rehabilitation, which has produced the poster "Uncertainty-Aware Conversations in Stroke Rehabilitation," has been accepted for presentation at AI for Science 2025 (AIS25)  
* **five PhD students are working in the projects: Samuele Tonati**, (Phd student of National Phd on AI supported by Institutional funds of SNS) working on RA1/RA4  on “*Ensamble counterfactual methods for Churn Analysis*”; **Clara Punzi**, (Phd student of National Phd on AI on Institutional funds of SNS) working on RA1 on learning to abstain and XAI; **Antonio Leitao** (Phd student of Computational Methods supported by Institutional funds of SNS ) working il RA1 on learning to abstain and XAI“; **Iacopo Colombini** (Phd student of Computational Methods on Institutional funds of SNS) working on RA2/RA4 working on mathematical foundation of XAI and XAI and Generative AI for mobile data;  **Gabriele Barlacch**i (Phd student of National Phd on AI on Institutional funds of SNS) working on RA1/RA2 creating a simulation environment to explore mechanistic explanations of recommendations to better understand the coevolution of human-machine interaction.

**SNS** also contributed with **Gizem Gezici, assistant professor**, was recruited by SNS in November 2022 with a background on natural language processing and was partially working on the project. She is working on RA2, exploring knowledge injection into the production of explanations in the context of text data type, on this she is co-supervising PhD student Paulo Bruno Serafim, focused on exploring how LLM might contribute to enhancing explanations \[69\][^9] which extension has been published in ECML-PKDD2025. She is also contributing to the use case in health care. She has also been tutoring students for the PhD course: Explainable AI, 20 hours of lectures, 20 hours of laboratory activities and projects at SNS. 

**2.1.2 CNR: Team members and their activities in the RP**

CNR in the RP, the following researchers have been taken part of the research:

* **Salvatore Rinzivillo was** responsible for the CNR Unit and R3 line and was involved in the design of the XAI library and *watchdog platform*. In this period, CNR worked in collaboration with SNS to improve the structure of the XAI Library and related algorithm, adding optimization to improve performance and quality of explanations. The XAI methods have been enriched with specific visual interfaces, summarized in the paper[^10]. He is also supervising the PhD thesis of Eleonora Cappuccio on visual XAI  
* **Mirco Nanni** and **Luca Pappalardo** are mostly involved in experimenting with the XAI methods on Mobility and on Well Being domains, where explainability is used within simulation contexts. In particular, Luca Pappalardo collaborates with Giovanni Mauro at SNS on the topic “The Urban Impact of AI: Modeling Feedback Loops in Next-Venue Recommendation”, aimed at formalizing the mechanistic understanding of Human-AI coevolution, and with Margherita Lalli at SNS on a similar topic related to the online markets domain.

CNR has also contributed with other resources to the project covered by other Institutional funds.  **Daniele Fadda**, a research fellow contract covered by CNR, with expertise on user-interface design that has contributed to the development for the XAI-library, and for developing and curating the project web-site, supporting communication for the dissemination events. **Andrea Beretta**, (XAI postdoc grant since August 2020- September 2024\) and now a research fellow contract at CNR. He has curated the interactions with the ethical mentor and with the CNR ethical approval.    
The team is also empowered by the postdoc **Carlo Metta** ( research fellow contract at  CNR), working to the extension of ABELE for health images and curating the various experiences on health we are pursuing in the project. PhD student **Eleonora Cappuccio (**grant on Institutional funds**)** working on making more expressive, through various visual metaphors, the explanation formats produced by LORE and other XAI Algs. 

**2.1.3 UNIPI: Team members and their activities in the RP**  
UNIPI: Other than the co-PI **Dino Pedreschi** involved in supervising all RAs other permanent researchers and professors are involved: 

* **Riccardo Guidotti**, a researcher at UniPI, is responsible for RA1 aimed at algorithms for local explanation, he is the main author of the algorithm named LORE capable of producing local explanation in the form of factual and counterfactual logic rules, and method ABELE that moves the generation of explanations into a latent space to produce exemplars and counter-exemplars for images and LASTS on time-series. He is the co-supervisor of Martina Cinquini, Marta Marchiori, Isacco Beretta, and Andrea Fedele, finishing or about to finish in this last RP, and bringing many valuable publications. Publications in RP are \[107,108,109, 110,111,112,113,114, 115, 116\].  
* **Salvatore Ruggieri** full professor at UniPI, is responsible for RA2: languages for expressing explanations in terms of expressive logic rules (with statistical and causal interpretation); He is the supervisor of Laura State on topics related to Declarative Reasoning on Explanations and developed the paradigm REASONX[^11]. He is also co-supervising Isacco Beretta and Martina Cinquini on topics at the crossroad of XAI and causality[^12].  
* **Anna Monreale**, Associate Professor at UniPI, is responsible for RA5: Ethics and Legal Impacts. She is the supervisor of PhD students Valerio Bonsignori and Luca Corbucci on topics at the crossroad of federated learning, explainability, and privacy. Publication in the last  RP are \[109, 116,117\].  
* **Mariarita Pierotti,** Associate Professor at UNIPI, has been involved in the project to analyze the importance and effectiveness of the use of XAI techniques for machine learning models in financial applications.  
* **Giorgio Ghelli**, full professor at UNIPI, has been involved in the project to study the possible formalisms to store explanations in databases with a particular focus on JSON format that is the most commonly used by Python-based models and methods benign the current standard of XAI approaches.  
* **Paolo Maria Mancarella**, full professor at UNIPI, has been involved in the project due to previous works on computational logic, particularly on developing systems capable of reasoning not only deductively but also hypothetically and predictively. Such research can support the development of AI capable of justifying its decisions in a transparent and user-friendly way.

The postdocs working in project in the RP are:

* **Simone Piaggesi has been recruited on XAI grant on May 2023**. He has taken the responsibility to continue the work on Interpretable Latent Space. He is the major responsible for the novel proposal ILLUME[^13] and in RA4 he has been working in the team for ILLUME[^14] as  “XAI4Science” tool by applying it to complex biomedical problems, specifically in pharmacology and cancer research. He collaborates with expert biomedical scientists to show how ILLUME can provide valuable insights and new hypotheses where explanation is often more crucial than prediction. He is part of the team that has proposed the PoC ILLUME4Science.

* **Francesco Spinnato**, (**on XAI grant since February 2024 till August 2025**) working on RA1  since the beginning of his thesis on “Explanation Methods for Sequential Data Models” with many papers following up including the excellent journal publication in \[57\][^15] (Dec 2024). 


One PhD student has an XAI grant on the RP: **Andrea** **Fedele,** who focuses on a method to explain the outcomes of Siamese Networks in the context of few-shot learning for audio data. Other students are: **Marta Marchiori Manerba,** focusing on using explainability for discrimination discovery. I**sacco Beretta** and **Martina Cinquini** are focusing on Causality and XAI, and **Luca Corbucci** is focusing on Explainability in Federated Learning.

In the reporting period there have been three visitors:

Period from 20 to 25 July 2025 for Prof. Ricardo Baeza Yates  
 Period from 8 to 21 June 2025 for Prof. James Brusseau,  
 Period from 28 of April to 31 May 2025 for Prof. Miquel Mirò Nicolau,

UNIPI has also contributed with other resources to the project covered by  Institutional funds.  **Mattia Setzu,** **XAI grant since April 2022,** and now a research fellow contract at UNIPI  contributes to RA1 mainly with extensions and use of one of the most relevant algorithms: GLOCALX, extending it at the meso level.  **Francesca Naretto**, (XAI PhD grant since November 2020\) and now a research fellow contract at UNIPI working on RA1 and RA5, since the beginning of the project with a thesis on “*The relationship between privacy and explanations*” summarized by the excellent journal publication in Transaction on Data Privacy 2025\[117\][^16], she has contributed to the LORE extension in several directions and now she is also exploring XAI in the case of federated architectures.
